newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand started the new year on a weak footing on Thursday as local importer and London-based dollar demand nudged it almost two cents weaker against the dollar.
It settled at 4.6985/7035 at 1400 GMT compared with 4.6800/6850 on Tuesday. All South African markets were closed on Wednesday for the New Year's Day holiday.

Dealers said the currency was under pressure from the start when importers began buying dollars. Weakness on the local bond market in reaction to losses on the U.S. Treasury bond market on Tuesday did not do much to help the rand either.
The initial demand took the rand to 4.6860 by late morning where dealers said London-based banks joined the fray.

"We saw demand from local importers and speculators. The usual suspects out of London were buying dollars," a dealer said. There was scant supply of dollars from exporters who were largely absent from the market.
"Around 4.70 there was talk of the Reserve Bank stopping it," the dealer added.
Volumes on the day were generally thin with most players' attention fixed on the first day of the second cricket Test being played between India and South African in Cape Town, dealers said.
Dealers said the rand's weaker bias was expected to remain on Friday amid further importer and speculative dollar demand.
The rand/pound cross regained some composure after starting the day at over eight against the British currency. It touched 8.0254 in the morning session.
However, cable's retracement from over $1.71 -- a four year high -- to around $1.6950 in the European afternoon helped the rand retrace to 7.9631/9763 by the finish.
Against the Deutschmark, the rand weakened to 0.3282/3288 from 0.3317/3323 previously.
On the bond market, offshore and local jobber selling pushed yields nearly 20 basis points higher on the back of weakness on the U.S. Treasury bond market and the softer rand.
The key 30-year U.S. Treasury bond yield rose to 6.64 percent on Tuesday from 6.54 before.
The local benchmark gilt -- the R150 -- was last quoted at a 16.24 percent after touching an intraday high of 16.28 percent earlier.
Traders said trade on the day had been very quiet with volumes described as modest.
On the money market three-month NCD rates were steady at between 17.40 and 17.75 percent while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at 16.70 to 17.00 percent.
The money market shortage stood at 10.448 billion rand on Tuesday from 10.737 billion rand on Monday.
Bond Exchange statistics showed foreigners sold a net 43.85 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying a net 128.06 million rand on Monday.
Nominal cumulative turnover was 562.4 million rand on Tuesday from 35.03 billion rand on Monday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
